fixed.q: The ______ design is a high-abstraction version of a system that is followed by ______ design that breaks the concept into a less-abstracted view of sub-systems, and later the ______ design showcases the implementation at module level.
fixed.w: Design goes from system design (most abstract) to architectural design (sub-systems) to detailed design (module level).

fixed.q: In building software, ______ should preferably be lower and ______ is preferred to be on the higher side.
o: inheritance from parent class, dependency with peer classes
aggregation with peer components, composition among classes
coupling among components, cohesion in bonding components
fixed.w: Good design aims for low coupling between components and high cohesion within them.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a graphical representation of an algorithm?
fixed.w: A flowchart is a graphical representation of an algorithm.

fixed.q: Which of the following symbols of a flow chart represents the processing phase?
fixed.w: A rectangle represents a process or processing step; a diamond is a decision, a parallelogram is I/O and an oval is start/end.

fixed.q: Which of the following is the easiest to be transformed into a computer program?
fixed.w: Pseudo-code is closest to real code, so it is the easiest to convert into a program.

fixed.q: Program links with other parts of the program in a flowchart are represented by ______.
fixed.w: Connectors (circles) link a flowchart to other parts of the program.

fixed.q: Which statements are true about sequence structure during program execution? I. Each statement is executed once II. No statement is repeated III. The statements are executed in any order
fixed.w: In a sequence structure each statement runs once, none is repeated, and the order is fixed. So I and II.

fixed.q: Two modules are said to be common coupled in software design if ______.
o: they share same global data areas
they communicate through an elementary data item
they communicate via a composite data
fixed.w: Common coupling means modules share the same global data area.

fixed.q: A module of a software is said to be logically cohesive if ______.
o: all the elements of the module perform similar operations like error handling, data input etc
if the set of functions of the module are all part of a procedure
different elements of the module cooperate to achieve a single function for example managing an employee's pay roll
all the elements of the module performs different operations alternatively
fixed.w: Logical cohesion: elements perform logically similar operations, such as all error handling or all input.

fixed.q: Rearrange the steps involved in top-down design programming: I. Analyze the problem; II. Revise and resequence; III. Write the main module; IV. Connect the modules in proper order; V. Write the remaining modules.
fixed.w: Top-down design: analyse the problem, write the main module, write the remaining modules, connect them, then revise and resequence.

fixed.q: The term in the MVC architecture that receives events is called ____.
fixed.w: The controller receives user events and input and updates the model and view.

fixed.q: In the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture, the model defines the ____.
fixed.w: The model holds the application's data and business rules. The view is the presentation layer.

fixed.q: In the context of modular software design, which one of the following combinations is desirable?
fixed.w: Good modules are internally focused (high cohesion) and loosely connected to each other (low coupling).

fixed.q: Where is GO TO not used?
fixed.w: Nassi-Shneiderman (structogram) diagrams represent only structured constructs (sequence, selection, iteration), so they cannot express GO TO.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a desirable property of a module?
fixed.w: Good modules are independent (low coupling, high cohesion).

fixed.q: ______ activities are at the very core of project completion work tasks, whereas ______ activities are not mandatory.
fixed.w: Functional activities are core to project completion; non-functional ones are not mandatory.

fixed.q: Which of the following identifies, controls, audits and reports modifications that invariably occur while software is being developed and after it has been released to a customer?
fixed.w: Software Configuration Management identifies, controls, audits and reports changes throughout the software's life.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a risk management methodology?
fixed.w: Risk can be accepted, avoided, transferred or mitigated; 'risk generation' is not a methodology.

fixed.q: CMM stands for:
fixed.w: CMM = Capability Maturity Model (SEI), with five maturity levels.

fixed.q: Which of the following software is used by a wide range of industries for project planning, resource allocation and scheduling?
fixed.w: Project management software (e.g. MS Project) handles planning, resource allocation and scheduling.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) 'Communications', 'Schedules' and 'Task lists' are key functionality aspects of project management software to guide your decision. ii) A data warehouse is a relational database that is designed for query and analysis rather than transaction processing. iii) Software integration option is one of the criteria for selecting project management software.
fixed.w: All three statements are true.

fixed.q: Which of the following projects deals with developing a well-understood application program, where the size of the development team is reasonably small and the team members are experienced in developing similar types of projects?
fixed.w: COCOMO 'organic' projects have small, experienced teams and well-understood applications.

fixed.q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding software metrics in software engineering? I. Direct measures of the software product include functionality quality, efficiency etc. of the software. II. Indirect measures of the software product includes lines of code produced, execution speed, memory size etc. of the software product.
fixed.w: The statements are swapped: LOC, speed and memory size are direct measures, while functionality, quality and efficiency are indirect. Neither is correct.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements are not true about CASE tool? I. It degrades the quality II. Reduce the drudgery in software engineer's work III. Increase maintenance cost
fixed.w: CASE tools improve quality and reduce maintenance cost, so I and III are not true. II is a real benefit.

fixed.q: Process of recovering the design and the requirement specification of a product from an analysis of its code is called as _______.
fixed.w: Recovering design and specification from the code is software reverse engineering.

fixed.q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding software project management? I. PERT charts can be derived automatically form Gantt charts. II. Gantt charts cannot be automatically derived from PERT charts.
fixed.w: A Gantt chart can be derived from a PERT chart, but a PERT chart cannot be derived from a Gantt chart because Gantt has no dependency information. Both statements as written are wrong.

fixed.q: Changes made to the system to reduce the chances of future system failure are called ____.
fixed.w: Preventive maintenance heads off future failures. Corrective fixes bugs, adaptive handles environment changes, and perfective adds improvements.

fixed.q: By open-domain CASE tools we mean
o: software packages to aid each phase of systems analysis and design which can be downloaded free of cost from the internet
tools available in the open domain
software packages which can be downloaded from the internet
fixed.w: Open-domain CASE tools are free, downloadable packages that support the analysis and design phases.

fixed.q: If P is the risk probability and L is the loss, then Risk Exposure (RE) is computed as
fixed.w: Risk exposure = probability × loss (Pressman).

fixed.q: Pareto principle advocates
fixed.w: The Pareto principle is the 80–20 rule (e.g. 80% of defects come from 20% of modules).

fixed.q: Which of the following software quality factors refers to the degree to which the software makes optimal use of system resources as indicated by the sub-attributes time behaviour and resource behaviour?
fixed.w: Efficiency (ISO 9126) covers time behaviour and resource behaviour.

fixed.q: Which of the following refers to a system test that forces a software to fail in a variety of ways and verifies that recovery is properly performed?
fixed.w: Recovery testing forces the software to fail in different ways and checks that recovery is performed properly.

fixed.q: In which debugging approach, the program is loaded with print statements to print the intermediate values with the hope that some of the printed values will help to identify the statement as error?
fixed.w: Brute-force debugging scatters print statements through the program to trace intermediate values.

fixed.q: What is the other name of White-box testing?
fixed.w: White-box testing is also called glass-box (clear-box) testing.

fixed.q: What is the full form of SQA in software engineering?
fixed.w: SQA = Software Quality Assurance.

fixed.q: Which of the following is not a part of the Test Implementation and Execution phase?
o: Creating test suites from the test cases
Executing test cases either manually or by using test execution tools
fixed.w: Test design belongs to the earlier analysis and design phase.

fixed.q: The black box software testing method focuses on the:
fixed.w: Black-box testing checks behaviour against the specification, using techniques such as boundary-value analysis. Control structure and cyclomatic complexity belong to white-box testing.
There are 4 decision points (while, if, else-if, final if), so V(G) = 4 + 1 = 5.

fixed.q: Defects are less costly if detected in which of the following phases?
fixed.w: The earlier a defect is found (requirements), the cheaper it is to fix.

fixed.q: In ______ testing only the functionality of the software module is tested.
fixed.w: Black-box testing checks functionality only, without looking at internal code.

fixed.q: Within software engineering, which prescriptive model is INCOMPATIBLE with circumstances in which the requirements alter throughout development?
fixed.w: Linear (waterfall) models assume fixed requirements, so they cannot cope with changes during development.

fixed.q: Which of the following process models are the oldest software engineering paradigms and suggest a linear process flow that is often inconsistent with modern realities?
fixed.w: Sequential (waterfall) models are the oldest paradigms, with a linear flow.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT true about the Waterfall model?
fixed.w: 'High cost' is the statement that is NOT true of the waterfall model.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a phase of the RAD model?
fixed.w: RAD phases are business, data and process modelling, application generation, and testing and turnover; 'development modelling' is not one.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid Software Life Cycle Model?
fixed.w: JAD, iterative and prototype are recognised models or methods; 'circular' is not.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is/are true for the Waterfall Model? i) This model does not work smoothly if there are some issues left at the previous step. ii) It projects the process of development in a cyclic manner, repeating every step after every cycle of the software development life cycle process. iii) This model considers risk, which often goes unnoticed by most other models. iv) This model provides means of testing of software at each stage in a reverse manner.
fixed.w: Only i is true. The waterfall model is linear (not cyclic), doesn't handle risk (that's spiral), and the V-model is the one that tests in reverse.

fixed.q: Spiral model of software development is also known as ______.
fixed.w: Boehm's spiral model is called a meta-model because it can contain other models.

fixed.q: In ______ model, software is developed in a series of incremental releases. I. Spiral II. Sequential
fixed.w: The spiral model develops software as a series of incremental releases (evolutionary); the sequential (waterfall) model doesn't.

fixed.q: Software consists of ____.
fixed.w: The standard SE definition: software = programs + documentation + operating procedures.

fixed.q: The SRS document produced at the end of requirement analysis and specification is known as ______.
fixed.w: The SRS describes what the system does, not how, so it is a black-box specification.

fixed.q: SRD stands for ____.
fixed.w: SRD is Ross and Schoman's Structured Requirements Definition technique. (Solved answer; some keys print A.)

fixed.q: A Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document should avoid discussing which one of the following?
fixed.w: An SRS says what the system must do, not how; design belongs in the design document (GATE 2015).

fixed.q: Which SDLC model is best when risk analysis is most important?
fixed.w: The spiral model (Boehm, 1986) repeats four quadrants per loop, with risk analysis as a key quadrant.

fixed.q: The spiral model was proposed by:
fixed.w: Boehm proposed the spiral model in 1986. Royce described the waterfall model in 1970.

fixed.q: The waterfall model is suitable when:
o: Requirements are well understood and stable
Users need to see a working model early
The project is high-risk and innovative
fixed.w: Waterfall is linear and sequential, so it needs fixed, clear requirements.

fixed.q: The V-model pairs each development phase with a:
fixed.w: V-model (verification and validation): requirements ↔ acceptance testing, design ↔ system/integration testing, coding ↔ unit testing.

fixed.q: In Scrum, a fixed time-boxed iteration is called a:
fixed.w: A sprint is usually 1–4 weeks long. Roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team.

fixed.q: RAD (Rapid Application Development) mainly relies on:
o: Reusable components and short development cycles
fixed.w: RAD uses component reuse, prototyping and a short cycle (about 60–90 days).

fixed.q: The level at which an organisation's processes are "optimising" in CMM is:
fixed.w: CMM levels: 1 Initial, 2 Repeatable, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimising.

fixed.q: "The system shall respond within 2 seconds" is a:
fixed.w: Performance, security, reliability and usability are non-functional requirements. Functional requirements say what the system does.

fixed.q: The IEEE standard for the SRS document is:
fixed.w: IEEE 830 is the recommended practice for SRS. 802 is LANs and 754 is floating point.

fixed.q: An SRS document should NOT contain:
fixed.w: An SRS says WHAT the system must do, not HOW it will be built.

fixed.q: The most desirable type of cohesion is:
fixed.w: Best to worst: functional, sequential, communicational, procedural, temporal, logical, coincidental.

fixed.q: The best (lowest) type of coupling is:
fixed.w: Best to worst: data, stamp, control, external, common, content. Good design aims for low coupling and high cohesion.

fixed.q: A Level-0 DFD is also called the:
fixed.w: The context diagram shows the whole system as one process with external entities and data flows.

fixed.q: Which UML diagram shows the order of messages between objects over time?
fixed.w: Sequence diagrams have lifelines and time-ordered messages. Class diagrams show static structure.

fixed.q: In a use case diagram, an external entity that interacts with the system is an:
fixed.w: Actors (stick figures) are users or external systems that interact with use cases.

fixed.q: Cyclomatic complexity of a control flow graph with E edges, N nodes and P connected components is:
fixed.w: V(G) = E − N + 2P (P = 1 for one program). It also equals decisions + 1, the number of independent paths.

fixed.q: Black-box testing is also called:
fixed.w: Black box tests the input–output behaviour without looking at the code. White (glass) box testing uses the internal structure.

fixed.q: Boundary value analysis is a:
fixed.w: BVA and equivalence partitioning are black-box techniques. Statement, branch and path coverage are white-box.

fixed.q: Testing done by the users at the developer's site is:
fixed.w: Alpha testing is at the developer's site; beta testing is at the customer's site by real users.

fixed.q: Re-testing after a change to make sure existing features still work is:
fixed.w: Regression testing checks that changes have not broken previously working functionality.

fixed.q: In top-down integration testing, missing lower-level modules are replaced by:
fixed.w: Top-down uses stubs (replace called modules). Bottom-up uses drivers (replace calling modules).

fixed.q: Maintenance done to adapt software to a new operating system or hardware is:
fixed.w: Corrective fixes bugs, adaptive handles a changed environment, perfective adds or improves features, preventive improves future maintainability.

fixed.q: In basic COCOMO, a small project with an experienced team and flexible requirements is:
fixed.w: COCOMO modes: organic (small and simple), semi-detached (medium), embedded (tight constraints, complex).

fixed.q: Function Point analysis measures software size based on:
o: The functionality delivered to the user
The number of lines of code
fixed.w: FP counts external inputs, outputs, inquiries, internal logical files and external interface files, independent of language.

fixed.q: In a PERT/CPM network, the longest path from start to end is the:
fixed.w: Activities on the critical path have zero slack; any delay in them delays the whole project.

fixed.q: A Gantt chart is mainly used for:
fixed.w: A Gantt chart is a bar chart of activities over time.

fixed.q: PERT expected time with optimistic a, most likely m and pessimistic b is:
fixed.w: The standard deviation is (b − a)/6.

fixed.q: A bar chart showing tasks against a calendar timeline is a:
fixed.w: Gantt charts show schedule and progress; PERT shows dependencies.

fixed.q: COCOMO is used for:
fixed.w: Basic COCOMO: Effort = a(KLOC)ᵇ person-months; modes are organic, semi-detached and embedded.

fixed.q: In COCOMO, small projects by experienced teams with familiar requirements are:
fixed.w: Embedded projects have tight hardware and operational constraints.

fixed.q: Modifying software to fix bugs found after delivery is:
fixed.w: Adaptive = adjusting to a new environment; perfective = new features or performance; preventive = improving future maintainability.

fixed.q: The best kind of module cohesion is:
fixed.w: Best to worst: functional, sequential, communicational, procedural, temporal, logical, coincidental.

fixed.q: The most desirable kind of coupling between modules is:
fixed.w: Aim for low coupling and high cohesion. Content coupling is the worst.

fixed.q: Which UML diagram shows the interaction between users (actors) and the system?
fixed.w: A sequence diagram shows messages between objects over time.

fixed.q: A Data Flow Diagram at level 0 is also called the:
fixed.w: It shows the whole system as one process with external entities.

fixed.q: Testing based on internal code structure (paths, branches) is:
fixed.w: Black-box testing uses only the specification: equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis.

fixed.q: Testing by customers at the developer's site is ___ testing; at the customer's own site, ___ testing.
fixed.w: Both are forms of acceptance testing.

fixed.q: Testing the system beyond its normal load to find its breaking point is:
fixed.w: Recovery testing forces failures to check that the system recovers.

fixed.q: The correct order of testing levels is:
fixed.w: Integration can be top-down (using stubs) or bottom-up (using drivers).

fixed.q: Cyclomatic complexity of a flow graph with E edges and N nodes is:
fixed.w: It also equals the number of decision points + 1.

fixed.q: Which model is best when requirements are unclear and users need to see a working model early?
fixed.w: Waterfall needs stable, well-understood requirements.

fixed.q: Which model was proposed by Barry Boehm and focuses on risk analysis in each loop?
fixed.w: Each loop: objectives, risk analysis, development, planning.

fixed.q: In the V-model, each development phase has a matching:
fixed.w: Also called the verification and validation model.

theory.SDLC & process models:
• Waterfall (Royce 1970): linear, fixed requirements, no going back.
• Prototype: unclear requirements, show a working model early.
• Incremental/iterative: deliver in parts. RAD: reuse, short cycle.
• Spiral (Boehm 1986): risk-driven, four quadrants per loop.
• V-model: each development phase has a matching test phase.
• Agile/Scrum: sprints (1–4 weeks), product backlog, Product Owner, Scrum Master, daily stand-up. XP: pair programming, TDD.
• CMM levels: 1 Initial, 2 Repeatable, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimising.
theory.Requirements & SRS:
• Functional (what the system does) vs non-functional (performance, security, usability, reliability).
• Elicitation: interviews, questionnaires, observation, JAD, prototyping, use cases.
• SRS (IEEE 830): correct, unambiguous, complete, consistent, verifiable, modifiable, traceable; says WHAT, not HOW.
• Feasibility: technical, economic, operational, schedule.
theory.Design (modularity, cohesion, UML, chart:
• Good design: high cohesion, low coupling.
• Cohesion best → worst: functional, sequential, communicational, procedural, temporal, logical, coincidental.
• Coupling best → worst: data, stamp, control, external, common, content.
• DFD: level 0 = context diagram; symbols for process, data store, external entity and data flow. Structure chart shows the module hierarchy.
• UML structural: class, object, component, deployment, package. Behavioural: use case, activity, state, sequence, collaboration/communication.
• Top-down vs bottom-up design; abstraction, information hiding, modularity.
theory.Testing:
• Verification (are we building the product right?) vs validation (are we building the right product?).
• Black box: equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis, cause-effect, decision table. White box: statement, branch, path coverage, cyclomatic complexity V(G) = E − N + 2P = decisions + 1.
• Levels: unit → integration (top-down with stubs, bottom-up with drivers, big-bang) → system → acceptance (alpha at developer site, beta at user site).
• Regression (after changes), smoke, stress, load, performance testing.
• Error → fault (bug) → failure.
theory.Maintenance & project management:
• Maintenance: corrective (bugs), adaptive (new environment), perfective (new features, performance), preventive (future maintainability). Perfective usually takes the largest share.
• Estimation: LOC, function points (inputs, outputs, inquiries, internal files, external interfaces), COCOMO (organic, semi-detached, embedded).
• Scheduling: Gantt chart, PERT (three time estimates), CPM (critical path = longest path, zero slack).
• Risk management: identification, analysis, planning, monitoring. Configuration management: version control, change control.
• Re-engineering and reverse engineering apply to legacy systems.
